color.description: The colour the chip draws, as any CSS colour the page can resolve. Empty is a legal value and is the NO COLOUR chip: it draws a slashed square rather than nothing, because a blank square in a palette reads as a white swatch and picking it would be picking white.

value.description: What the swatch stands for: the detail of the select it dispatches, and what a swatch group compares its own value against. Empty falls back to color, so a palette of literal colours needs no second attribute; set it when the swatch stands for a TOKEN whose colour is only how it looks, which is the case a project's palette is made of.

label.description: The swatch's name, and its accessible name: it is written to aria-label, so it wins over anything slotted beside the chip. A COLOUR IS NOT A NAME. Without this the element falls back to the value and then to the colour, which announces "#3b82f6" one character at a time — legible, technically a name, and useless. Give every swatch in a palette the word a reader would use for it.

checked.description: Empty for a plain button; true or false for one member of a swatch group, which then carries role=radio and aria-checked on its control and puts role=none on the HOST so the radio is the group's own child rather than a grandchild behind a generic. jx-swatch-group is the single writer of this on its children, exactly as jx-tabs is of a tab's selected, so a host moves the selection by writing the group's value.

selected.description: Draws the chosen ring and the tick without announcing anything, for a swatch a host has chosen outside a radio group. It is the drawing alone: checked is what a reader is TOLD, and setting one never sets the other.

disabled.description: Cannot be chosen or focused. Disabled, never absent.

size.description: sm, md or lg. The chip grows; the button's target does not shrink below the kit's control height, so a small swatch is still a target a finger can hit.

tabindex.description: Forwarded to the inner control as its tabindex, which is what makes a roving caret possible: the focusable node is the button inside, not the host, so a group moving focus writes this rather than reaching into a child's internals. It is a PROPERTY ONLY and deliberately not an observed attribute: written as an attribute it would land on the host as well, and a host carrying tabindex is itself focusable, so one control would become two tab stops.

inkOf.description: Black or white, whichever can be seen on the swatch's own colour, or the empty string for a colour only the browser can resolve. Pure: it takes the colour and returns a word.

emits.name: select
emits.description: The swatch was activated; detail is what it stands for. A swatch group listens for it and answers with its own change.

onClick.description: Activation says what the swatch stands for and nothing else. It does not write its own checked: inside a group the group owns that, and outside one the host does, and an element that chose itself would disagree with both.

& [part=\"chip\"].$description: The ring is drawn with the ink the element worked out from its own colour rather than with a neutral border token, because a mid-grey boundary disappears against a mid-grey swatch and a control whose edge cannot be seen is a WCAG 1.4.11 failure. The checkerboard behind it is what makes a translucent colour read as translucent instead of as a paler opaque one.

&[data-empty] [part=\"chip\"].background: linear-gradient(to bottom right, transparent calc(50% - 1px), var(--jx-danger) calc(50% - 1px), var(--jx-danger) calc(50% + 1px), transparent calc(50% + 1px)), var(--jx-bg-input)
